subject: Post-demo alignment: Trial framing & owners — Lumina Systems
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.inference>
To: Elliot Simmons <elliot@luminasystems.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta@luminasystems.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-07T15:05:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo alignment: Trial framing & owners — Lumina Systems

Thanks for the time today — great conversation. Per our demo, I wanted to capture a concise trial (POC) framing so we can align on success criteria, timeline, and owners before the technical kickoff. Below is a proposed plan — please flag anything missing or off by EOD Wednesday.

Summary of what we demoed:
- Redwood API for conversational search indexing + retrieval-augmented generation
- Dedicated trial workspace: private model variant + isolated dataset for evaluation

Proposed trial goals (3-week lightweight evaluation):
1) Retrieval precision: top-3 answers are relevant to user queries in >= 75% of sampled queries (50 queries across two verticals)
2) Latency: median token generation latency <= 220 ms at 1 qps sustained
3) Cost baseline: candidate config should reduce per-session token cost vs current baseline by >= 30% while preserving quality
4) Integration verification: end-to-end flow (ingest -> indexing -> query -> render) works with your auth and data routing

High-level timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): align success metrics, sign trial charter, access provisioning (3 business days)
- Week 1: ingestion & baseline test runs (Ben lead)
- Week 2: model tuning (quantization/batching), evaluation runs, metric collection
- Week 3: wrap, comparison report, executive recap

Ownership:
- Commercial / Program lead: Naomi Feldman (I will own scope, POC charter, trial acceptance)
- Technical lead (integration & tests): Ben Carter
- Onboarding / runbook & ops: Marissa Cole

Attachments: I attached a short POC charter and an evaluation checklist. Drive folder with shared test data and a HubSpot deal link are below.

Immediate asks for Lumina team:
- Confirm the success criteria above or propose adjustments
- Provide a primary technical contact for provisioning (SSH keys/service account)
- Share any restricted test dataset constraints (PII, retention)

Next steps:
- If you agree, I’ll send a formal charter and an NDA addendum (if needed) and book the provisioning slot for Friday.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.inference
[Attachment: lumina-poc-charter.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]
From: Elliot Simmons <elliot@luminasystems.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.inference>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta@luminasystems.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-08T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo alignment: Trial framing & owners — Lumina Systems

Thanks Naomi — this looks useful and aligned. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Success criteria: the retrieval precision metric makes sense; can we define the sampling methodology (50 queries: 30 actual support queries + 20 product discovery)? Also, can we add a subjective quality check: mean relevance score from two SME raters >= 3.5/5?
2) Latency: 220 ms median sounds good, but can we add a 95th percentile SLA target as well (<= 400 ms)?
3) SOC2 / Security: procurement will need SOC2 documentation and a brief on data separation for the dedicated workspace. Can you attach the SOC2 summary or point to where it lives?

Tech contact for provisioning: Marta Ruiz (marta@luminasystems.com). She’ll own keys and data ingestion. 

If those items look OK, we can confirm and lock the Friday provisioning slot.

—Elliot
Elliot Simmons
Director of Product, Lumina Systems
elliot@luminasystems.com
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.inference>
To: Elliot Simmons <elliot@luminasystems.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta@luminasystems.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-08T12:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo alignment: Trial framing & owners — Lumina Systems

Appreciate the quick feedback, Elliot — good call on the sample breakdown and the 95th percentile SLA. I’ve updated the proposed criteria below and attached the revised checklist.

Updated success criteria (final proposal):
- Retrieval precision: >= 75% top-3 relevance across 50 queries (30 support + 20 discovery).
- Subjective quality: mean relevance score across two SME raters >= 3.5/5.
- Latency: median <= 220 ms; 95th percentile <= 400 ms at 1 qps sustained load.
- Cost: >= 30% token cost reduction vs your current baseline for a standard support session (we’ll provide the cost model template).

Security docs: SOC2 summary & data separation overview: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bLuminaPOC (I also attached the short SOC2 executive summary). If procurement wants the full report we can arrange an NDA and a secure share.

Provisioning plan (Friday slot):
- Pre-provision checklist (Marta) — send service account + ingestion sample by Thursday EOD
- Provisioning window (Ben) — Friday 10:00–12:00 PT: set up workspace, ingest small sample, verify auth
- Baseline smoke tests — Friday afternoon: quick end-to-end checks

Deliverables we’ll share during the trial:
- Weekly status note + results dashboard (token counts, latencies, relevance samples)
- Final comparison report with metric breakdown and suggested config for production

If that matches your expectations I’ll: 1) update the POC charter and resend, 2) create the HubSpot task + invite calendar events for the provisioning window.

Thanks — Naomi
[Attachment: lumina-eval-checklist.xlsx]
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.inference>, Elliot Simmons <elliot@luminasystems.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta@luminasystems.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo alignment: Trial framing & owners — Lumina Systems

Quick note from the tech side — we’re good to run the Friday provisioning. I’ll prepare the ingestion script and a short baseline test suite (50 queries as discussed).

Request for Marta: can you confirm the format of the sample data (CSV vs JSON) and whether the dataset includes any fields we should mask? If there’s PII please mark the columns and we’ll apply the masking step during ingestion.

I’ll post the baseline test results to the shared Drive folder after Friday’s run and leave a short readme with how to reproduce.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
